questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of salts do alkali metals form with oxo-acids?
questions.solution: Alkali metals typically form sulfate salts with oxo-acids. For example, sodium sulfate and potassium sulfate are common alkali metal sulfate salts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What ion is formed when aluminium hydroxide dissolves in excess of alkali?
questions.solution: Aluminium hydroxide dissolves in excess of alkali to give aluminate ion, [Al(OH)<sub>4</sub>]-.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When beryllium (Be) reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl), what is the product formed?
questions.solution: Beryllium (Be) reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl) to form beryllium chloride (BeCl<sub>2</sub>) and hydrogen gas (H<sub>2</sub>).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why do the alkaline earth metals have higher melting and boiling points than the corresponding alkali metals?
options: Due to the presence of more protons
Due to their lower ionization energies
questions.solution: The alkaline earth metals have larger atomic sizes compared to the alkali metals in Group 1, which leads to stronger metallic bonding and higher melting and boiling points.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the paramagnetic nature of alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia when they stand for some time?
questions.solution: Paramagnetic alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia become diamagnetic when they stand for some time.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are the primary uses of sodium chloride?
options: It is used as a cleaning agent
It is used as a food preservative
It is used as a fuel additive
It is used as a construction material
questions.solution: Sodium chloride is primarily used as a common salt or table salt for domestic purposes and as a food preservative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary reason for sodium having lower reducing power compared to lithium?
questions.solution: Sodium (Na) has lower reducing power compared to lithium (Li) primarily due to its higher ionization enthalpy. Higher ionization enthalpy means it is less likely to lose an electron and act as a reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is sodium hydroxide generally prepared commercially?
options: By heating sodium metal with oxygen
By the reaction of sodium with water
By the electrolysis of sodium chloride in a Castner-Kellner cell
By the combination of sodium and chlorine gas
questions.solution: Sodium hydroxide is generally prepared commercially by the electrolysis of sodium chloride in a Castner-Kellner cell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which gas is evolved at the anode during the electrolysis of sodium chloride to produce sodium hydroxide?
questions.solution: Chlorine gas is evolved at the anode during the electrolysis of sodium chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of compounds do alkali metals readily form when they react with halogens?
questions.solution: Alkali metals readily react with halogens to form ionic halides, where the metal cation (M+) and halogen anion (X-) are held together by electrostatic attraction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary reason for the alkaline earth metals being strongly electropositive in nature?
questions.solution: The alkaline earth metals are strongly electropositive in nature due to their low ionization energies, which means they readily lose electrons to form positive ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the significance of the low melting and boiling points of alkali metals?
options: They are excellent conductors of electricity
questions.solution: The low melting and boiling points of alkali metals allow them to readily conduct electricity in their molten or dissolved state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal nitrate crystallizes with six molecules of water?
questions.solution: Magnesium nitrate crystallizes with six molecules of water, forming Mg(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>·6H<sub>2</sub>O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the outermost orbital electron of an alkali metal when it is exposed to a flame during a flame test?
options: It moves to a lower energy level
It gets excited to a higher energy level
It is ejected from the atom
questions.solution: When an outermost orbital electron of an alkali metal is exposed to a flame during a flame test, it gets excited to a higher energy level due to the heat from the flame.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal forms superoxides when it reacts with oxygen?
questions.solution: Potassium forms superoxides when it reacts with oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which group of elements exhibits similar behavior in terms of low melting and boiling points as alkali metals?
questions.solution: Noble gases also have low melting and boiling points, similar to alkali metals, due to weak van der Waals forces between their atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which factor primarily determines the solubility of alkaline earth metal sulfates in water?
questions.solution: The solubility of alkaline earth metal sulfates in water is primarily determined by the hydration enthalpy of the metal ions. Higher hydration enthalpies favor greater solubility in water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkaline earth metal halides, which ones are soluble in organic solvents?
questions.solution: All alkaline earth metal halides are ionic in nature except for beryllium halides, which are covalent and soluble in organic solvents.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the structure of the chlorides of beryllium and aluminium in the vapour phase?
questions.solution: Both the chlorides of beryllium and aluminium have Cl- bridged chloride structure in the vapour phase.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which group of elements in the periodic table has the largest atomic sizes within a given period?
questions.solution: Within a particular period of the periodic table, alkali metals have the largest atomic sizes. Atomic size decreases from left to right across a period, and alkali metals are located on the far left side of the periodic table.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal is known for its toxicity and is handled with caution in industrial settings?
questions.solution: Beryllium is known for its toxicity, and precautions must be taken when handling it in industrial settings.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the trend in melting points among alkali metals as you move down the periodic table?
questions.solution: The melting points of alkali metals generally decrease as you move down the periodic table, which is a consequence of weaker metallic bonding due to the increased atomic size and greater distance between the valence electrons and the nucleus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many water molecules are associated with each molecule of magnesium nitrate when it crystallizes?
questions.solution: Magnesium nitrate crystallizes with six molecules of water (hexahydrate) when it forms hydrates.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does calcium oxide (CaO) react with acidic oxides at high temperature?
options: It combines with them to form compounds.
questions.solution: Calcium oxide (CaO), being a basic oxide, combines with acidic oxides at high temperature to form compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkaline earth metal halides, which ones undergo hydrolysis when heated?
questions.solution: The corresponding hydrated halides of Beryllium and Calcium undergo hydrolysis when heated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is one of the uses of calcium carbonate in the field of cosmetics?
questions.solution: Calcium carbonate is used as a filler in cosmetics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among lithium and magnesium, which element reacts slowly with water and forms a nitride by direct combination with nitrogen?
questions.solution: Both lithium and magnesium react slowly with water and form nitrides, Li<sub>3</sub>N, and Mg<sub>3</sub>N<sub>2</sub>, by direct combination with nitrogen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is responsible for the change in color from blue to bronze in concentrated alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia?
options: Absorption of energy in the ultraviolet region
Change in the concentration of ammoniated electrons
questions.solution: The change in color from blue to bronze in concentrated alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia is due to a change in the concentration of ammoniated electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal halide forms a chain structure in the solid state?
questions.solution: Beryllium chloride (BeCl<sub>2</sub>) forms a chain structure in the solid state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkaline earth metal sulfates, which one has the lowest solubility in water?
questions.solution: Barium sulfate (BaSO<sub>4</sub>) has the lowest solubility in water among the alkaline earth metal sulfates. It is sparingly soluble and often forms a white precipitate when added to water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an oxo-acid?
questions.solution: Sulfuric acid (H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>) is an example of an oxo-acid because it contains oxygen atoms and has acidic protons attached to hydroxyl groups with oxo groups on the same sulfur atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of ion is stable only in the presence of large cations like K, Rb, Cs?
questions.solution: The superoxide (O2-) ion is stable only in the presence of large cations like potassium (K), rubidium (Rb), and cesium (Cs).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a common use of calcium?
questions.solution: Calcium is an essential mineral for the formation and maintenance of bones and teeth in humans.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ions is smaller than the parent atom among alkali metals?
questions.solution: Among alkali metals, the monovalent ions (M+) are smaller than the parent atom. This is because the loss of one electron results in a decrease in electron repulsion and a smaller ionic radius.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which compounds can be prepared using sodium chloride?
questions.solution: Sodium chloride can be used in the preparation of Na<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>, NaOH, and Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is calcium carbonate prepared through chemical reactions?
options: By passing oxygen through slaked lime
By adding sodium chloride to calcium carbonate
By passing carbon dioxide through slaked lime
By adding calcium carbonate to sodium chloride
questions.solution: Calcium carbonate can be prepared by passing carbon dioxide through slaked lime.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal has the highest melting point?
questions.solution: Beryllium (Be) has the highest melting point among the alkaline earth metals

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkaline earth metals, which element has the smallest atomic radius?
questions.solution: Among the alkaline earth metals, beryllium has the smallest atomic radius due to its higher nuclear charge and fewer electron shells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkaline earth metal sulfates, which one forms a white precipitate when added to water due to its low solubility?
questions.solution: Barium sulfate (BaSO<sub>4</sub>) forms a white precipitate when added to water due to its low solubility, making it useful for diagnostic imaging and other applications where a visible contrast is needed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which compound is an example of an extensively hydrated alkaline earth metal compound?
questions.solution: MgSO<sub>4</sub>·7H<sub>2</sub>O is an example of an extensively hydrated alkaline earth metal compound.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of solutions are formed when alkali metals dissolve in liquid water?
questions.solution: Alkali metals dissolve in liquid water to form colorless and non-conducting solutions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does the solubility of sodium chloride change with an increase in temperature?
questions.solution: The solubility of sodium chloride does not increase appreciably with an increase in temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal ion has the highest degree of hydration?
questions.solution: Among the alkali metal ions, Li+ has the highest degree of hydration. This means that it attracts and binds to a larger number of water molecules compared to the other alkali metal ions, making it the most hydrated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal has the highest enthalpy of formation for its oxide?
questions.solution: Strontium (Sr) has the highest enthalpy of formation for its oxide among the alkaline earth metals, making it very stable to heat.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which compound forms a hydrate among the following options?
questions.solution: Compounds of alkaline earth metals are more extensively hydrated compared to alkali metal compounds. MgCl<sub>2</sub> and CaCl<sub>2</sub> form hydrates, whereas NaCl and KCl do not.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal oxide is the least basic?
questions.solution: Beryllium oxide (BeO) is the least basic among the alkaline earth metal oxides. It is amphoteric, meaning it can react with both acids and bases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which group of elements do the alkaline earth metals belong to in the periodic table?
questions.solution: The alkaline earth metals are found in Group 2 of the periodic table.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal oxide is the least stable to heat?
questions.solution: Magnesium oxide (MgO) is the least stable to heat among the alkaline earth metal oxides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the stability of carbonates and hydrogen carbonates as you move down the alkali metal group in the periodic table?
options: The stability of both carbonates and hydrogen carbonates increases.
The stability of both carbonates and hydrogen carbonates decreases.
The stability of carbonates increases, but the stability of hydrogen carbonates decreases.
The stability of carbonates decreases, but the stability of hydrogen carbonates increases.
questions.solution: As you move down the alkali metal group in the periodic table, the electropositive character of the metals increases, leading to increased stability of both carbonates (M<sub>2</sub>CO3) and hydrogen carbonates (MHCO3).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does Plaster of Paris behave when mixed with water?
questions.solution: Plaster of Paris, when mixed with an adequate quantity of water, forms a plastic mass that hardens into a solid in a relatively short time.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What contributes to the reducing nature of beryllium (Be2+)?
questions.solution: The small size of Be2+ ion contributes to its reducing nature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, and barium, which metal is most readily attacked by air to form the oxide and nitride?
questions.solution: Barium is the most readily attacked by air among these metals and forms both the oxide and nitride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary use of Plaster of Paris in the medical industry?
questions.solution: Plaster of Paris is commonly used in the medical industry for immobilizing bone fractures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical formula of Gypsum?
questions.solution: Calcium sulfate has the chemical formula CaSO<sub>4</sub>·2H<sub>2</sub>O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary use of lime in the tanning industry?
questions.solution: Lime is primarily used in the tanning industry for removing hair from hides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal has the lowest melting point?
questions.solution: Sodium (Na) has the lowest melting point among the alkali metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which industry commonly uses milk of lime in its processes?
questions.solution: The textile industry commonly uses milk of lime in its processes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical formula for the nitrate formed by the dissolution of magnesium carbonate in dilute nitric acid?
questions.solution: When magnesium carbonate is dissolved in dilute nitric acid, it forms magnesium nitrate with four molecules of water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical formula of the dihydrogen liberated when an alkaline earth metal reacts with hydrochloric acid?
questions.solution: When an alkaline earth metal reacts with hydrochloric acid, it liberates dihydrogen gas, which has the chemical formula H<sub>2</sub>.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the common tendency of beryllium and aluminium ions regarding complex formation?
questions.solution: Beryllium and aluminium ions have a strong tendency to form complexes, specifically BeF<sub>4</sub>2- and AlF<sub>6</sub>3-.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term used to describe the distortion of the electron cloud of an anion by a cation?
questions.solution: The distortion of the electron cloud of an anion by a cation is called polarization.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of alkali metals in their oxides?
questions.solution: In the oxides of alkali metals, the oxidation state of the alkali metal is +1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the final product formed when alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia slowly liberate hydrogen?
questions.solution: Alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia slowly liberate hydrogen, resulting in the formation of amides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following trends is observed as you move down the group from Be to Ba in terms of electropositive character?
questions.solution: As you move down the group from Be to Ba, the electropositive character of the elements increases. This is because the ionization enthalpy decreases, making it easier for these elements to lose electrons and exhibit strong electropositive behavior.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What property of calcium hydroxide makes it suitable for use in white wash?
questions.solution: Calcium hydroxide is used in white wash due to its disinfectant nature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal sulfate has the highest hydration enthalpy?
questions.solution: Barium sulfate (BaSO<sub>4</sub>) has the highest hydration enthalpy among alkaline earth metal sulfates, which contributes to its lower solubility in water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary reason for the conducting nature of alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia?
questions.solution: The conducting nature of alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia is primarily due to the presence of ammoniated electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which property of beryllium (Be) contributes to its weaker reducing nature?
questions.solution: The small ionic radius of beryllium contributes to its weaker reducing nature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among lithium and magnesium, which one crystallizes from aqueous solution as the hydrate LiCl·2H<sub>2</sub>O?
questions.solution: Lithium chloride (LiCl) crystallizes from aqueous solution as the hydrate LiCl·2H<sub>2</sub>O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the product of the reaction between calcium (Ca) and hydrochloric acid (HCl)?
questions.solution: Calcium (Ca) reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl) to form calcium chloride (CaCl<sub>2</sub>) and hydrogen gas (H<sub>2</sub>).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many ammonia molecules are coordinated around the alkaline earth metal in the ammoniate ion?
questions.solution: In the ammoniate ion [M(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>6</sub>]2+, six ammonia molecules are coordinated around the alkaline earth metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the common name for anhydrous calcium sulfate formed when gypsum is heated?
questions.solution: The anhydrous calcium sulfate formed when gypsum is heated is commonly known as "dead burnt plaster."

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary reason for lithium's high negative E<sub>o</sub> value and strong reducing power?
questions.solution: Lithium's high negative E<sub>o</sub> value and strong reducing power are primarily due to its high hydration enthalpy, which is a result of its small ion size and strong electrostatic attraction with water molecules. This makes lithium an effective reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal is used in the production of fireworks to create a brilliant white light?
questions.solution: Strontium is used in fireworks to produce a brilliant white light.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why do beryllium and magnesium appear kinetically inert to oxygen and water?
options: They have a strong aversion to oxygen and water.
They have a protective oxide film on their surface.
questions.solution: Beryllium and magnesium have a thin oxide film on their surfaces that prevents further reaction with oxygen and water, making them appear kinetically inert.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds forms a hydrate?
questions.solution: MgCO<sub>3</sub> forms a hydrate. Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>, K<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>, and CaCO<sub>3</sub> do not form hydrates.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In concentrated alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia, what color does the solution change to?
questions.solution: In concentrated alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia, the blue color changes to bronze.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical equation for the reaction of calcium oxide with silicon dioxide to form calcium silicate?
questions.solution: The reaction of calcium oxide (CaO) with silicon dioxide (SiO<sub>2</sub>) to form calcium silicate is represented by the chemical equation 2CaO + SiO<sub>2</sub>  → 2CaSiO<sub>3</sub>.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What causes limewater to turn milky when carbon dioxide is passed through it?
questions.solution: When carbon dioxide is passed through lime water, it turns milky due to the formation of calcium carbonate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What characteristic colors do calcium, strontium, and barium impart to a flame?
questions.solution: Calcium imparts a brick red color, strontium imparts a crimson color, and barium imparts an apple green color to a flame due to the excitation and subsequent emission of electrons at different energy levels.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which technique is used for the determination of alkali metals by measuring the absorption of light at specific wavelengths?
questions.solution: Flame photometry is the technique used for the determination of alkali metals by measuring the absorption of light at specific wavelengths corresponding to the characteristic colors emitted by the alkali metals in a flame.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Both lithium and magnesium are known to be harder and lighter than other elements in their respective groups. Which property contributes to their hardness?
questions.solution: The hardness of lithium and magnesium is due to strong metallic bonding in their crystal structures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal is the most reactive towards acids?
questions.solution: Among the alkaline earth metals, Barium (Ba) is the most reactive towards acids due to its lower ionization energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For what purpose are the chlorides of beryllium and aluminium used?
questions.solution: The chlorides of beryllium and aluminium are used as Friedel-Craft catalysts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal halide has the highest number of water molecules in its hydrate?
questions.solution: Strontium chloride (SrCl<sub>2</sub>·6H<sub>2</sub>O) has the highest number of water molecules in its hydrate among the given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal oxide is sparingly soluble in water?
questions.solution: The oxides of alkaline earth metals, except for beryllium oxide, are basic and react with water to form sparingly soluble hydroxides. Magnesium oxide (MgO) is an example of such an oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In flame tests for alkali metals, why is it important to use an oxidizing flame?
options: To prevent the emission of characteristic colors
To provide the conditions for excitation of electrons
questions.solution: An oxidizing flame is used in flame tests for alkali metals because it provides the necessary conditions, including oxygen, to excite the outermost orbital electrons of alkali metal atoms, leading to the emission of characteristic colors.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of acids are the chlorides of beryllium and aluminium?
questions.solution: The chlorides of beryllium and aluminium are strong Lewis acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical process involved in the preparation of calcium oxide on a commercial scale?
options: Heating of limestone (CaCO<sub>3</sub>) in a rotary kiln
Combining calcium and oxygen at high temperature
Oxidation of calcium carbonate (CaCO<sub>3</sub>) with water vapor
questions.solution: Calcium oxide (CaO) is prepared on a commercial scale by heating limestone (CaCO<sub>3</sub>) in a rotary kiln at temperatures ranging from 1070 to 1270 K.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal ion has the strongest tendency to form hydrates in the presence of water?
questions.solution: Among the alkali metal ions, Li+ has the strongest tendency to form hydrates in the presence of water. It has a high degree of hydration due to its strong interaction with water molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal hydroxide is sparingly soluble in water and used as an antacid in medicine?
questions.solution: Magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)<sub>2</sub>) is sparingly soluble in water and is used as an antacid in medicine due to its ability to neutralize excess stomach acid. It forms a slightly soluble hydroxide in water, which helps alleviate acid-related digestive issues.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkali metals, which one has the lowest density?
questions.solution: Cesium (Cs) has the lowest density among the alkali metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term used to describe the process by which alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia slowly liberate hydrogen?
questions.solution: The process by which alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia slowly liberate hydrogen is a reduction reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical formula of lithium chloride dihydrate?
questions.solution: The chemical formula of lithium chloride dihydrate is LiCl·2H<sub>2</sub>O, indicating that it contains two water molecules per formula unit of lithium chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary reason for using the flame test for calcium, strontium, and barium?
options: To observe the temperature of the flame
To detect their characteristic colors in qualitative analysis
questions.solution: The flame test is used to detect the characteristic colors (brick red, crimson, apple green) of calcium, strontium, and barium, which aids in qualitative analysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal has the highest atomic number?
questions.solution: Cesium (Cs) has the highest atomic number among the alkali metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which compound is extensively hydrated?
questions.solution: Among the options provided, MgSO<sub>4</sub> is extensively hydrated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal sulfate has the smallest ionic charge on its metal ion?
questions.solution: Beryllium sulfate (BeSO<sub>4</sub>) has the smallest ionic charge on its metal ion (Be2+), which contributes to its unique properties and solubility in water despite its high lattice enthalpy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary factor responsible for beryllium's (Be) reducing nature?
options: Hydration energy associated with Be2+ ion.
questions.solution: Beryllium's reducing nature is primarily due to the large hydration energy associated with the small Be2+ ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is meant by the term "deliquescent" when describing sodium hydroxide crystals?
options: They are prone to melting easily
They readily absorb moisture from the air and dissolve
questions.solution: Deliquescent substances like sodium hydroxide crystals have the property of absorbing moisture from the air and dissolving in it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why does lithium, despite having the most negative E<sub>o</sub> value among the alkali metals, react less vigorously with water compared to sodium?
options: Lithium has a larger size and lower hydration energy.
Lithium has a smaller size and lower hydration energy.
Sodium has a larger size and higher hydration energy.
Sodium has a smaller size and higher hydration energy.
questions.solution: The less vigorous reaction of lithium with water, despite having a more negative E<sub>o</sub> value, is attributed to its small size and very high hydration energy, which makes it less reactive than sodium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a use of sodium carbonate?
questions.solution: Sodium carbonate is not used as an automobile fuel; it has various other industrial and domestic uses, such as water softening, laundering, cleaning, and glass manufacturing.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following best describes the change in magnetic behavior when alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia go from paramagnetic to diamagnetic?
questions.solution: The change in magnetic behavior when alkali metal solutions in liquid ammonia go from paramagnetic to diamagnetic means they become less magnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What products are formed when alkali metals react with water?
questions.solution: When alkali metals react with water, they produce hydroxide and hydrogen gas as the products.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which group of metals exhibits higher melting and boiling points compared to alkali metals?
questions.solution: Alkaline earth metals have higher melting and boiling points than alkali metals due to their smaller atomic sizes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What causes alkali metals to tarnish in dry air?
questions.solution: Alkali metals tarnish in dry air due to the formation of their oxides, which subsequently react with moisture in the air to form hydroxides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the given alkaline earth metal ions, which one is the largest in size?
questions.solution: As you move down the alkaline earth metal group, the ionic size increases. Among the options provided, Ba2+ is the largest ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which process is used to make nitrates from carbonates?
questions.solution: Nitrates are typically made by dissolving carbonates in dilute nitric acid, which is a common method to produce nitrates.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkaline earth metal oxides, which one has the highest melting point?
questions.solution: Magnesium oxide (MgO) has the highest melting point among the alkaline earth metal oxides, making it useful for high-temperature applications.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal does not form a solid hydrogencarbonate?
questions.solution: Lithium (Li) does not form solid hydrogencarbonates, unlike some other alkaline earth metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal oxide is amphoteric in nature?
questions.solution: Beryllium oxide (BeO) is amphoteric, meaning it can react with both acids and bases, unlike the oxides of other alkaline earth metals which are typically basic in nature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal forms peroxides when it reacts with oxygen?
questions.solution: Sodium forms peroxides (Na<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) when it reacts with oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among lithium hydroxide (LiOH) and magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)<sub>2</sub>), which one decomposes on heating?
questions.solution: Both lithium hydroxide (LiOH) and magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)<sub>2</sub>) decompose on heating.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkaline earth metals, which one readily reacts with acids to liberate dihydrogen?
questions.solution: Among the alkaline earth  metals, magnesium readily reacts with acids to liberate dihydrogen gas  according to the equation: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal forms the oxide CaO, which does not combine with excess oxygen to give any superoxide?
questions.solution: Calcium (Ca) forms the oxide CaO, which does not combine with excess oxygen to give any superoxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What characteristic color does barium impart to a flame during a flame test?
questions.solution: Barium imparts an apple green color to a flame during a flame test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal carbonate is sparingly soluble in water and often used as a dietary supplement for calcium?
questions.solution: Calcium carbonate (CaCO<sub>3</sub>) is sparingly soluble in water and is often used as a dietary supplement for calcium due to its low solubility.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which field is Plaster of Paris used for making casts of statues and busts?
questions.solution: Plaster of Paris is frequently used in sculpture to make casts of statues and busts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following elements is not an alkali metal?
questions.solution: Magnesium (Mg) is not an alkali metal; it is an alkaline earth metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the classification of carbohydrates based on their behavior on hydrolysis?
questions.solution: The classification of carbohydrates based on their behavior on hydrolysis is into three groups: monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, and polysaccharides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal exhibits the least reactivity with acids?
questions.solution: Beryllium is the least reactive among the alkaline earth metals when it comes to reacting with acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following nitrates crystallizes as an anhydrous salt?
questions.solution: Barium nitrate crystallizes as the anhydrous salt, which means it does not have associated water molecules in its crystal structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkali metal carbonates is known to be thermally stable and widely used in various applications, including in antacids?
questions.solution: Sodium carbonate (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>), also known as soda ash or washing soda, is thermally stable and widely used in various applications, including as an ingredient in antacids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary reason for the high electrical and thermal conductivities of alkaline earth metals?
options: Presence of free electrons in the metal lattice
questions.solution: The high electrical and thermal conductivities of metals are primarily due to the presence of free electrons in the metal lattice that can move freely and carry electrical and thermal energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the general trend in reactivity of alkali metals with water as you move down the group?
questions.solution: The general trend in reactivity of alkali metals with water is that it increases as you move down the group, with the lower alkali metals reacting more vigorously than the higher ones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkaline earth metals imparts a brick red color to a flame during a flame test?
questions.solution: Calcium imparts a brick red color to a flame during a flame test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkaline earth metals, which one is most readily attacked by air to form the oxide and nitride?
questions.solution: Calcium is readily attacked by air to form the oxide (CaO) and nitride (Ca<sub>3</sub>N<sub>2</sub>).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What trend is observed in the tendency of alkaline earth metal nitrates to form hydrates with increasing size of the metal?
options: Hydrate formation increases with increasing size
Hydrate formation decreases with increasing size
There is no clear trend in hydrate formation
Hydrate formation is independent of the size of the metal
questions.solution: The passage mentions a decreasing tendency to form hydrates with increasing size of the alkaline earth metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the characteristic color of solutions formed when alkaline earth metals dissolve in liquid ammonia?
questions.solution: Alkaline earth metals form deep blue-black solutions when dissolved in liquid ammonia, indicating the presence of ammoniated ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does sodium hydroxide behave when dissolved in water?
options: It forms a weak alkaline solution
It does not dissolve in water
It forms a strong alkaline solution
questions.solution: Sodium hydroxide is readily soluble in water to form a strong alkaline solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why are alkaline earth metals considered strong reducing agents?
options: They have large positive reduction potentials.
They have large negative reduction potentials.
questions.solution: Alkaline earth metals have large negative reduction potentials, indicating their ability to readily donate electrons and act as reducing agents.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Are the chlorides of beryllium and aluminium soluble in organic solvents?
questions.solution: The passage states that both the chlorides of beryllium and aluminium are soluble in organic solvents.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In qualitative analysis, which test can be used to detect the presence of calcium, strontium, and barium ions?
questions.solution: The flame test is helpful in detecting the presence of calcium, strontium, and barium ions in qualitative analysis by observing the characteristic colors they impart to a flame.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>) recovered in the Solvay Process?
options: By passing CO<sub>2</sub> through a solution of sodium chloride
By treating the solution containing NH<sub>4</sub>Cl with Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub>
questions.solution: In the Solvay Process, ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>) is recovered by treating the solution containing NH<sub>4</sub>Cl with calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub>).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which analytical techniques are commonly used to determine the concentration of alkali metals in a sample?
options: Flame Photometry and Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy
questions.solution: Flame photometry and atomic absorption spectroscopy are commonly used analytical techniques to determine the concentration of alkali metals in a sample.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal ion has the largest ionic size?
questions.solution: Among the given options, Sr2+ is the largest alkaline earth metal ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal halide has the formula MgCl<sub>2</sub>·8H<sub>2</sub>O?
questions.solution: The formula MgCl<sub>2</sub>·8H<sub>2</sub>O represents hydrated magnesium chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the overall change represented by the standard electrode potential (E<sub>o</sub>) for reducing power?
questions.solution: The standard electrode potential (E<sub>o</sub>) for reducing power represents the overall change in the process, which includes sublimation enthalpy, ionization enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy. Among these, the hydration enthalpy plays a significant role in determining the reducing power of alkali metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of flame is typically used in flame tests for alkali metals?
questions.solution: An oxidizing flame is typically used in flame tests for alkali metals because it provides the necessary conditions for the excitation of the outermost orbital electrons and the emission of characteristic colors.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why do beryllium and magnesium not impart any color to a flame during a flame test?
questions.solution: Beryllium and magnesium have electrons that are too strongly bound to get excited by a flame, so they do not impart any color to the flame during a flame test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What ion is formed when beryllium hydroxide dissolves in excess of alkali?
questions.solution: Beryllium hydroxide dissolves in excess of alkali to give a beryllate ion, [Be(OH)<sub>4</sub>]2-.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are the products of the reaction between alkali metals and gaseous ammonia?
questions.solution: The reaction between alkali metals and gaseous ammonia typically results in the formation of ammonium hydride and nitrogen gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are oxo-acids, and where is the acidic proton located in them?
options: Oxo-acids are acids containing oxygen atoms. The acidic proton is typically on a hydroxyl group attached to an oxo group on the same atom.
Oxo-acids are acids derived from oxides. The acidic proton is located on a hydroxyl group bonded to a different atom.
Oxo-acids are acids that lack oxygen atoms. The acidic proton is located on a hydroxyl group attached to a carbon atom.
Oxo-acids are acids formed by oxidation reactions. The acidic proton is located on a hydroxyl group attached to a nitrogen atom.
questions.solution: Oxo-acids are acids that contain oxygen atoms, and the acidic proton is usually found on a hydroxyl group (OH) attached to an oxo group (a double-bonded oxygen) on the same atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which statement best explains why the atomic and ionic radii of alkaline earth metals are smaller than those of the corresponding alkali metals in the same periods?
options: Alkaline earth metals have more electrons than alkali metals.
Alkaline earth metals have a higher nuclear charge than alkali metals.
Alkaline earth metals have a higher electron affinity than alkali metals.
Alkaline earth metals have a lower ionization energy than alkali metals.
questions.solution: The atomic and ionic radii are determined by the balance between the attractive force of the nucleus and the repulsive force between electrons. Alkaline earth metals have more protons in their nuclei compared to alkali metals, leading to a stronger nuclear charge and smaller atomic/ionic radii.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal halide would be expected to have the most ionic character?
questions.solution: Sodium fluoride would be expected to have the most ionic character among these options because sodium (Na+) has a larger ionic radius compared to lithium (Li+), leading to stronger ionic bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the carbon dioxide produced during the preparation of calcium oxide?
options: It is trapped within the solid structure of calcium oxide.
It is released into the atmosphere.
It is used in other chemical reactions.
It is removed to allow the reaction to proceed to completion.
questions.solution: The carbon dioxide produced during the preparation of calcium oxide is removed as soon as it is produced to enable the reaction to proceed to completion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At what temperature is gypsum heated to obtain Plaster of Paris?
questions.solution: Gypsum (CaSO<sub>4</sub>·2H<sub>2</sub>O) is heated to 393 K to obtain Plaster of Paris.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to gypsum (CaSO<sub>4</sub>·2H<sub>2</sub>O) when it is heated to 393 K?
options: It decomposes to form anhydrous calcium sulfate
questions.solution: When gypsum is heated to 393 K, it loses water of crystallization and forms anhydrous calcium sulfate (CaSO<sub>4</sub>).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which industry is sodium carbonate commonly used?
questions.solution: Sodium carbonate is commonly used in the glass and soap manufacturing industries.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal forms an oxide and nitride when burned in air?
questions.solution: When burned in air, magnesium forms both magnesium oxide (MgO) and magnesium nitride (Mg<sub>3</sub>N<sub>2</sub>).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkaline earth metal carbonates, which one has the highest thermal stability?
questions.solution: Strontium carbonate (SrCO3) has the highest thermal stability among the alkaline earth metal carbonates. The thermal stability increases with increasing cationic size.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal forms a peroxide when it reacts vigorously with oxygen?
questions.solution: Sodium forms a peroxide (Na<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) when it reacts vigorously with oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal oxide reacts with water to form a sparingly soluble hydroxide?
questions.solution: Beryllium oxide (BeO) is the only alkaline earth metal oxide that does not react with water to form a sparingly soluble hydroxide. All the other alkaline earth metal oxides, including magnesium oxide (MgO), calcium oxide (CaO), and strontium oxide (SrO), react with water to form sparingly soluble hydroxides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal sulfate is known for its low solubility and use as a radiopaque contrast agent in medical imaging?
questions.solution: Barium sulfate (BaSO<sub>4</sub>) is known for its low solubility and is used as a radiopaque contrast agent in medical imaging procedures such as X-rays and CT scans.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which field is Plaster of Paris used for ornamental work?
questions.solution: Plaster of Paris is used in dentistry for ornamental work and dental molds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Besides the manufacture of soap and textiles, name one other industrial application of sodium hydroxide.
questions.solution: Sodium hydroxide is used in water treatment processes as well as in various other industrial applications.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the common structure of the monoxides (MO) formed by alkaline earth metals?
questions.solution: The monoxides (MO) formed by alkaline earth metals, except for BeO, have a rock-salt structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical formula for quicklime?
questions.solution: Quicklime is chemically represented by CaO.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal burns with dazzling brilliance in air?
questions.solution: Magnesium burns with dazzling brilliance in air due to its high reactivity with oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal has the highest melting point?
questions.solution: Among the alkali metals, lithium (Li) has the highest melting point.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among alkali metal halides, which one is the most covalent in nature?
questions.solution: Among alkali metal halides, lithium iodide is the most covalent in nature due to the high polarizing ability of the small lithium ion and the larger size of the iodide anion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: As you move down the group of alkaline earth metals, what happens to the tendency to form halide hydrates?
questions.solution: The tendency to form halide hydrates gradually decreases down the group of alkaline earth metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which of the following industries is sodium hydroxide commonly used?
options: Textile industries for mercerizing cotton fabrics
questions.solution: Sodium hydroxide is commonly used in the textile industries for mercerizing cotton fabrics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal forms a monoxide when it burns in oxygen?
questions.solution: Lithium forms a monoxide (Li<sub>2</sub>O) when it burns in oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the purpose of sodium hydrogen carbonate in fire extinguishers?
options: To release oxygen to support combustion
To generate carbon dioxide to smother the fire
To create a barrier to prevent the spread of fire
questions.solution: Sodium hydrogencarbonate is used in fire extinguishers to generate carbon dioxide (CO<sub>2</sub>), which displaces oxygen and helps smother the fire by removing the oxygen necessary for combustion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What causes alkali metals to impart characteristic colors to an oxidizing flame?
questions.solution: Alkali metals impart characteristic colors to an oxidizing flame because the heat from the flame excites the outermost orbital electron to a higher energy level, and when it returns to the ground state, radiation in the visible spectrum is emitted due to the presence of multiple valence electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How are alkali metals typically stored to prevent their reaction with air and water?
questions.solution: Alkali metals are normally kept in kerosene oil to prevent their reaction with air and water due to their high reactivity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary role of sodium hydrogencarbonate as an antiseptic for skin infections?
options: Killing bacteria on the skin's surface
questions.solution: Sodium hydrogen carbonate can act as a mild antiseptic for skin infections by killing bacteria on the skin's surface.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal oxide is the most stable to heat?
questions.solution: Strontium oxide (SrO) is the most stable to heat among the alkaline earth metal oxides. As you move down the group, the thermal stability of the oxides generally increases, and strontium oxide is the most stable to high temperatures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What property of alkali metals makes them strong reducing agents?
questions.solution: The high reducing power of alkali metals is primarily attributed to their high hydration enthalpy. This is because the small size of alkali metal ions, such as lithium (Li+), results in strong electrostatic attraction with water molecules, leading to a highly negative standard electrode potential (E<sub>0</sub>) and strong reducing properties.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of solutions are formed when alkali metals dissolve in liquid ammonia?
questions.solution: Alkali metals dissolve in liquid ammonia to form deep blue solutions that are conducting in nature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the appearance of calcium oxide?
questions.solution: Calcium oxide (CaO) is a white amorphous solid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why is lithium carbonate (Li<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>) less stable to heat compared to other alkali metal carbonates?
options: Lithium carbonate is inherently less stable due to its composition.
Lithium carbonate is more stable to heat than other alkali metal carbonates.
Lithium carbonate decomposes into Li<sub>2</sub>O and CO<sub>2</sub> when heated due to its small size polarizing CO<sub>3</sub>2- ions.
Lithium carbonate does not undergo any thermal decomposition.
questions.solution: Lithium carbonate (Li<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>) is less stable to heat because lithium ions, being very small in size, polarize the carbonate ion (CO<sub>3</sub>2-), leading to the formation of more stable lithium oxide (Li<sub>2</sub>O) and carbon dioxide (CO<sub>2</sub>) when heated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What role does the atomization enthalpy of a metal play in its reducing nature?
options: Higher atomization enthalpy increases reducing power.
Lower atomization enthalpy increases reducing power.
Atomization enthalpy does not affect reducing power.
Atomization enthalpy is inversely related to reducing power.
questions.solution: A higher atomization enthalpy increases the reducing power of a metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which step in the overall change of alkali metal reduction has the highest energy requirement?
options: Formation of metal ions in aqueous solution
questions.solution: The ionization of the metal (formation of metal ions) typically requires the highest energy input in the overall process of alkali metal reduction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkaline earth metal hydroxides, which one has the highest solubility in water?
questions.solution: Barium hydroxide (Ba(OH)<sub>2</sub>) has the highest solubility in water among the alkaline earth metal hydroxides. As you move down the group, the solubility of the hydroxides increases, and barium hydroxide is the most soluble due to its position at the bottom of the group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal hydroxide is the most basic?
questions.solution: Barium hydroxide (Ba(OH)<sub>2</sub>) is the most basic among the alkaline earth metal hydroxides. As you move down the alkaline earth metal group in the periodic table, the basicity of the hydroxides increases, and barium hydroxide has the highest basic character due to its position at the bottom of the group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are the natural forms in which calcium carbonate occurs?
questions.solution: Calcium carbonate occurs naturally in forms such as limestone, chalk, and marble.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why are calcium chloride (CaCl<sub>2</sub>) and magnesium chloride (MgCl<sub>2</sub>) considered impurities in crude sodium chloride?
options: They are highly toxic to humans
They easily absorb moisture from the atmosphere (deliquescent)
They cause the salt to become discolored
questions.solution: Calcium chloride and magnesium chloride are considered impurities in crude sodium chloride because they are deliquescent, meaning they absorb moisture easily from the atmosphere.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the remarkable property of Plaster of Paris when mixed with water?
options: It forms a plastic mass that hardens
questions.solution: Plaster of Paris forms a plastic mass that gets into a hard solid when mixed with water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What effect does increasing atomic size have on the melting and boiling points of alkali metals?
questions.solution: Increasing atomic size generally leads to higher melting and boiling points in alkali metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the relationship between standard electrode potential (E<sub>o</sub>) and reducing power for alkali metals?
options: Higher E<sub>o</sub> indicates higher reducing power.
Higher E<sub>o</sub> indicates lower reducing power.
E<sub>o</sub> and reducing power are not related.
E<sub>o</sub> remains constant for all alkali metals.
questions.solution: In the context of alkali metals, a more negative standard electrode potential (E<sub>o</sub>) indicates higher reducing power. So, higher E<sub>o</sub> values correspond to lower reducing power.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal sulfate has the largest ionic radius?
questions.solution: Barium sulfate (BaSO<sub>4</sub>) has the largest ionic radius among alkaline earth metal sulfates due to the larger size of the barium ion (Ba2+).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why are the fluorides of alkaline earth metals relatively less soluble than the chlorides?
options: Due to their lower lattice energies
Due to their higher lattice energies
questions.solution: The fluorides of alkaline earth metals are relatively less soluble than the chlorides because they have higher lattice energies.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What property of beryllium and aluminium makes them not readily attacked by acids?
options: Presence of a oxide film on the surface
questions.solution: Both beryllium and aluminium are not readily attacked by acids due to the presence of an oxide film on the surface of the metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal has the highest boiling point?
questions.solution: Cesium has the highest boiling point among the alkali metals due to its larger atomic size and stronger metallic bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal sulfate has the smallest ionic radius?
questions.solution: Beryllium sulfate (BeSO<sub>4</sub>) has the smallest ionic radius among alkaline earth metal sulfates due to the smaller size of the beryllium ion (Be2+).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When strontium (Sr) reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl), which gas is liberated?
questions.solution: Strontium (Sr) reacts with hydrochloric acid to liberate hydrogen gas (H<sub>2</sub>) as a product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a use of Plaster of Paris?
questions.solution: Plaster of Paris is not used in cement production.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal sulfate has the highest lattice enthalpy?
questions.solution: Beryllium sulfate (BeSO<sub>4</sub>) has the highest lattice enthalpy among the alkaline earth metal sulfates due to the strong electrostatic attractions between the beryllium ions and sulfate ions in its crystal lattice.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal hydroxide can react with acid and alkali to form soluble salts?
questions.solution: Beryllium hydroxide (Be(OH)<sub>2</sub>) is amphoteric in nature, meaning it can react with both acids and alkalis to form soluble salts. This property sets it apart from the other alkaline earth metal hydroxides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the suspension of slaked lime in water known as?
questions.solution: The suspension of slaked lime in water is known as milk of lime.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal appears somewhat grayish and is harder than the other alkaline earth metals?
questions.solution: Beryllium appears somewhat grayish and is harder than the other alkaline earth metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which property contributes to the non-systematic trend in the melting and boiling points of certain metals compared to alkali metals?
questions.solution: The non-systematic trend in the melting and boiling points of certain metals compared to alkali metals is primarily due to differences in atomic size. Smaller-sized atoms tend to have higher melting and boiling points due to stronger metallic bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary reason for the explosive reaction of potassium with water?
questions.solution: The explosive reaction of potassium with water is primarily due to its low ionization energy, which allows for a rapid release of energy and ignition of hydrogen gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry

options: Ability to lose electrons when irradiated with light

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens if there is an excess of carbon dioxide during the preparation of calcium carbonate?
options: It leads to the formation of sodium carbonate
It leads to the formation of calcium hydroxide
It leads to the formation of calcium hydrogencarbonate, which is water soluble
It leads to the formation of calcium chloride

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary reason for the low melting and boiling points of alkali metals?
options: Weak metallic bonding due to a single valence electron
questions.solution: The low melting and boiling points of alkali metals can be attributed to their weak metallic bonding, which is primarily due to the presence of only a single valence electron in each atom. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among lithium chloride (LiCl) and magnesium chloride (MgCl<sub>2</sub>), which one is soluble in ethanol?

No, they are insoluble in water.
Their solubility varies depending on the temperature.
They are only soluble in non-polar solvents.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.solution: Magnesium is commonly used in the production of lightweight alloys in aerospace and automotive industries due to its low density and good mechanical properties.

options: To increase acidity in baked goods
To provide a source of hydrogen gas during baking

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Property of the alkaline earth metals that increases with their atomic number
options: solubility of their hydroxides in water
solubility of their sulphates in water
questions.solution:
Electronegativity as well as ionisation energy both usually decrease on moving downward a group with increase in atomic number. The hydroxides and sulphates of alkaline earth metals are ionic solids and the solubility of ionic solids is governed by two factors, viz, lattice energy and hydration energy. For solubility, hydration energy > lattice energy.
Hydration energy varies inversely with size, ie, decreases with increase in size. However, lattice energy in case of sulphates, remains almost same with increase in the atomic number of alkaline earth metals, due to large size of sulphate ion. Hence, hydration energy only governs the solubility in this case. Thus, solubility of alkaline earth metal sulphates decreases as the hydration energy decreases on moving downward the II A group.
On the other hand, in case of hydroxides, the lattice energies are different because of medium size of hydroxide ions, and decreases on moving from $\mathrm{Be}$ to $\mathrm{Ba}$. This tends to increase the solubility and to overcome the counter-effect produced by the decrease in hydration energy. Hence, the solubility of alkaline earth metal hydroxides increases with increase in the atomic number of alkaline earth metals.

questions.q: Which of the following is only acidic in nature?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ in aqueous medium coordinates a molecule of water to form the hydrated species
In this species, $\mathrm{B}^{3+}$ ion, because of its small size, exercises a high polarizing power thereby pulling the sigma electron charge of the coordinated $\mathrm{O}$ atom towards itself. The coordinated oxygen, in turn, pulls the sigma electron charge of the $\mathrm{OH}$ bond of the attached $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ molecule towards itself. This facilitates the removal of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ion from the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond, as shown below.
Thus the solution of $\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ in water acts as a weak acid. That is why it reacts with $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution to produce the sodium salt. \begin{aligned} \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_3+\mathrm{NaOH} \rightleftharpoons & \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Na}^{+}\left[\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_4\right]^{-} \\ \rightleftharpoons & \mathrm{Na}^{+} \mathrm{BO}_2^{-}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ & \text { sodium } \\ & \text { metaborate } \end{aligned}
